summary: RAG few-shot with semantic NLEmbedding retrieval
hypothesis: Replacing Jaccard word-overlap retrieval with on-device NLEmbedding cosine similarity would surface better-matched few-shot exemplars and improve coverage, because exp003's gains came from well-matched demonstrations and Jaccard's near-zero matches on topically distinct queries were leaving quality on the table.
technique: Swapped exp003's Jaccard word-overlap exemplar retrieval for on-device NLEmbedding sentence-embedding cosine similarity, so the 2 injected few-shot demonstrations are the nearest task-type match even with zero shared vocabulary — everything else in the single FM call pipeline remained identical.
result: Scored 0.273 on dev-10 (0 wins / 0 ties / 10 losses vs Sonnet), down 0.047 from the exp003 best of 0.320 and losing exp003's lone tie; rubric atom=4, spec=3, cover=3, nat=3, nonRed=3. Coverage stayed flat at 3 and the same failure modes recurred verbatim, falsifying the hypothesis — better-matched exemplars did not move the coverage wall, confirming that retrieval/prompt-quality levers alone cannot overcome the 3B's which-unknowns-matter judgment gap. Discarded.
